verdict.rationale: GrowthBook's targeting docs describe rules with conditions evaluated against SDK-passed attributes such as user ID, country, plan type, or any custom property. They also name saved groups as reusable targeting segments. Rules can be layered on a feature so different users get different values, for example a forced value for beta testers above a gradual rollout. missing for 10: in-depth documentation of saved groups (only named once), independent or hands-on corroboration of attribute-based targeting (the runtime probe only evaluated a default value).

support.subject: As a developer, I can target flags with attribute-based rules and reusable segments so the right users see the right variation

citations.quote: Target feature flags with user attributes, conditions, saved groups, and percentage rollouts.
Conditions are evaluated against **attributes** you pass into the SDK — like user ID, country, plan type, or any custom property.
Layer multiple rules on one feature to compose behavior — for example, a forced value for beta testers above a gradual rollout to everyone else.
All SDKs use the same assignment logic, so the same attributes always produce the same variation regardless of which SDK you use.
